question.problem:
What is the first term that exceeds $2\,000\,000$ in the following geometric sequence?

$$
4,\,28,\,196,\,1\,372,\,…
$$
question.worked_solution:
The first term of the sequence is ${a}_{1}=4$ and the common ratio is

$$
r=\frac{28}{4}=7.
$$

So, the $n$th term of the sequence can be written as:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{n-1} \\  & =4\cdot {7}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$

We want the $n$th term to be greater than $2\,000\,000.$
Hence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & >2\,000\,000 \\ 4\cdot {7}^{n-1} & >2\,000\,000 \\ {7}^{n-1} & >500\,000 \\ \operatorname{log}⁡({7}^{n-1}) & >\operatorname{log}⁡(500\,000) \\ (n-1)\operatorname{log}⁡(7) & >\operatorname{log}⁡(500\,000) \\ n-1 & >\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(500\,000)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(7)} \\ n & >\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(500\,000)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(7)}+1\end{aligned}
$$

Estimating the right-hand side using a calculator, we get:

$$
\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(500\,000)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(7)}+1≈7.744
$$

Therefore, the $8$th term is the first term of the sequence that exceeds $2\,000\,000.$
